statement: A Git discovery ceiling only stops Git walking up from the scanned directory; it cannot stop a .git file or directory inside that directory. Refusing uploaded .git metadata and confining discovery are therefore two independent controls, and each needs its own guard deletion: with the ceiling in place but the .git rule deleted, an uploaded gitdir file still disclosed a synthetic host repository's commit SHA and tracked file name. The same run showed a leak test must be able to fail on every leak it asserts: the enclosing-repository fixture could leak only the SHA, so the file-name assertion lives where that leak occurs.
